limits: Introductory chapter: no experiments, datasets or measured results; all numbers are illustrative or cited biology.
Proofs are asserted ('it can be shown'), not given.

Dated: ReLU is described as 'recently' the neuron of choice (2017-era book); calls ReLU 'restricted linear unit' (usual name rectified linear unit; the cited Nair and Hinton title says Rectified); softmax, tanh-over-sigmoid advice stays valid.
Defers training (gradient descent, backprop) to Chapter 2 and ReLU pitfalls to Chapter 5.
practices: Prefer tanh over sigmoid when an S-shaped nonlinearity is used, because tanh is zero-centered (p13).
Use a softmax output layer when labels are mutually exclusive and a probability distribution is wanted (p15).
Hidden layers usually have fewer neurons than the input to force compressed representations (p11).
Do not stack linear neurons only; use nonlinearity or hidden layers add nothing (p12-13).
Inspect hidden-layer activations to see what features the network learned (p11).
Express layers as y = f(W^T x + b) with W of size n x m so they map to matrix operations in software (p12).
